newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trade on Wednesday on profit-taking mainly from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,388 yuan ($409) per tonne, losing seven yuan. It opened at a low of 3,380.
May fell 50 yuan to 3,380, July rose 90 to 3,300, September shed 35 to 3,313 and the January 1998 contract two to 3,390.
Combined volume fell to 11,200 tonnes from 21,300.
Soybeans opened lower and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
"Retail investors dominated today's trading with most of them liquidating their positions for quick profit due to the uncertain market direction," one trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate around current levels in the next few days.
